messages:
maria: FYI — got consolidated support tickets from three customers asking for streaming tool/function calls with partial structured outputs. Main ask: start consuming tool results before the full response completes, and ensure the stream can be validated as structured JSON chunks.

devin: Customer A (Acme) — needs incremental tool outputs to feed their live UI; cannot wait for final token. Billing milestone in 6 weeks.

devin: Customer B (BetaCorp) — using function-calling heavily, wants each tool call to emit structured events as they arrive. Also asked for resume/replay if stream drops.

jules: Sales here — two deals might close faster if we ship a pilot. They want an estimated timeline and risk list to include in proposals.

alex: Eng-ML perspective — key challenges: 1) keeping KV cache consistent when interleaving tool outputs, 2) making partial JSON pieces safe to parse (no half-broken objects), 3) ensuring function call semantics (one call -> one canonical result).

sam: Eng-runtime — we can implement framed streaming events (start/chunk/end) and an "is_final" marker. Main cost: additional serialization steps and slightly higher p95 due to flush boundaries. Rough perf hit 5-10% p95 in worst case.

maria: Proposed initial scope (beta):
- Wire format: explicit event types for tool-call lifecycle (tool_call.start, tool_call.chunk, tool_call.end).
- Payloads are JSON envelopes; each envelope is a standalone valid JSON object when possible.
- Final envelope contains full validated object and "is_final":true.
- Backwards compatibility: if client does not opt into streaming, default to existing single-response behavior.

maria: Acceptance criteria for pilot:
- SDKs (node/python) can receive and reconstruct tool events incrementally.
- Final reconstructed object validates against provided schema.
- Stream failure mode documented with deterministic fallback (replay or full-response fallback).
- Pilot customers integrated and passing validation on their test prompts.

alex: Example minimal event sequence we propose: 
```
{ "type": "tool_call.start", "call_id": "abc123", "tool": "search" }
{ "type": "tool_call.chunk", "call_id": "abc123", "seq": 0, "payload": "{\\\"results\\\":[{\\\"id\\\":1}]" }
{ "type": "tool_call.chunk", "call_id": "abc123", "seq": 1, "payload": "...,\\\"more\\\":true}" }
{ "type": "tool_call.end", "call_id": "abc123", "is_final": true }
```
Note: payloads are double-escaped when embedded in the outer JSON, SDKs will unescape and assemble.

devin: Support requirement — customers want a resume token or offset to continue after transient network failures. Otherwise they ask for server-side replay to regenerate same stream.

sam: Runtime can add per-call sequence numbers and a resume token. That requires keeping short-lived persistence (offsets) or recomputation. Adds complexity and ~1-2% cost on write paths. We also need an idempotency header from clients, e.g., X-Request-Id.

maria: Risks: SDK churn (parsing/edge cases), telemetry and storage cost for partial events, schema mismatch between tool implementers. Mitigations: opt-in beta with a feature flag, tooling to validate schemas in Console, and defaulting to non-streaming behavior if validation fails.

jules: For sales — if we pick a no-resume initial pilot we can shave ~2 weeks off timeline. Is that acceptable for the customers who asked?

alex: Engineering estimate: spike/proof-of-concept 2w, core runtime + API 3w, SDK updates 2w, QA + pilot integration 1-2w. Total ~8w. If we do no-resume, we can target ~6w.

maria: Proposed rollout plan:
1) Approve beta scope (resume vs no-resume decision).
2) RFC with exact wire format + example SDK glue code (sam to draft).
3) Flagged beta rollout to 2 customers (Acme, BetaCorp) + opt-in in Console.
4) Collect telemetry and iterate.

sam: I'll own the RFC and be eng lead. Will open PR with proto + perf baseline this week.

devin: I'll prepare pilot intake docs, contact customers for test prompts and schema, and document failure modes.

triage-bot: Thread labeled P1 and assigned to product.

maria: Thanks — I'm going to capture ACs in the backlog item now and link this thread. If anyone has objections to the no-resume initial scope, raise them within 48h.
